t.3.16.1: Rāma, having performed his ablutions, together with Sītā and Saumitri, then went from that bank of the Godāvarī back to their own āśrama.
t.3.16.2: Having reached that hermitage, Rāghava, together with Lakṣmaṇa, performed the morning rites and then went to the leaf-hut.
t.3.16.3: The mighty-armed Rāma, seated in the leaf-hut together with Sītā, shone like the moon with the star Citrā. Together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa he held conversations on various topics.
t.3.16.4: Then, while Rāma sat there with his mind absorbed in conversation, a certain rākṣasī came by chance to that place.
t.3.16.5: She, named Śūrpaṇakhā, the sister of the ten-necked rākṣasa, approached Rāma and beheld him, who was like one of the thirty gods.
t.3.16.6: Him, lion-chested and mighty-armed, with eyes like lotus petals, tender of form yet of great courage, endowed with the marks of a king.
t.3.16.7: Seeing Rāma, dark as a blue lotus, radiant like Kandarpa and equal to Indra, the rākṣasī became bewildered with desire.
t.3.16.8: She, ugly-faced, beheld Rāma, fair of face; she, pot-bellied, him of slender waist; she, with misshapen eyes, him with large eyes; she, with copper-colored hair, him with beautiful hair.
t.3.16.9: She, ugly, approached him who was of pleasing form; she of terrible voice, him whose voice was sweet; she, old and dreadful, the youthful one; she of crooked speech, the upright one.
t.3.16.10: The rākṣasī, utterly wicked in conduct and hideous to behold, overcome by lust, spoke to Rāma, who was righteous in conduct and pleasing to the eye.
t.3.16.11: Wearing matted locks in the guise of an ascetic, accompanied by your wife and bearing bow and arrows, how have you come to this region frequented by rākṣasas?
t.3.16.12: Thus addressed by the rākṣasī Śūrpaṇakhā, the scorcher of foes, out of the straightforwardness of his mind, began to tell her everything.
t.3.16.13: There was a king named Daśaratha, whose valor was like that of the gods. I am his eldest son, known among the people by the name Rāma.
t.3.16.14: This is my younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa by name, devoted to me; and this is my wife, the princess of Videha, renowned as Sītā.
t.3.16.15: Constrained by the command of my father, the lord of men, and of my mother, I, longing for dharma, have come here to dwell in the forest for the sake of dharma.
t.3.16.16: I wish to know you; let it be told who you are and whose you are. And for what reason have you come here? Tell me truly.
t.3.16.17: Having heard his words, the rākṣasī, tormented by desire, said: “Listen, Rāma; I shall speak to you words of mine that are true in their meaning.”
t.3.16.18: I am a rākṣasī named Śūrpaṇakhā, able to take any form at will. Alone I roam this forest, striking fear into all.
t.3.16.19: My brother is the rākṣasa named Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas; and another is the mighty Kumbhakarṇa, who is ever sunk in deep sleep.
t.3.16.20: Vibhīṣaṇa, however, is righteous of soul and does not act like a rākṣasa; and the brothers Khara and Dūṣaṇa are renowned for their valor in battle.
t.3.16.21: Leaving them all behind, O Rāma, from the moment I first saw you I have come to you with love, to you, the best of men, as my husband. Be my husband for all time; what will you do with Sītā?
t.3.16.22: She is misshapen and ugly; this woman is no match for you. I alone am a wife fit for you in beauty; look at me!
t.3.16.23: This misshapen, wicked, hideous human woman with her sunken belly I shall devour, together with this brother of yours.
t.3.16.24: Then, my beloved, together with me you will roam the Daṇḍaka forests, gazing upon mountain peaks and woods of many kinds.
t.3.16.25: Thus addressed, Kākutstha, skilled in speech, laughed and began to speak these words to the woman with intoxicating eyes.
